doc.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025

title: How demo sessions worked and what they paid
summary: Demos came from a lead sheet, recorded in an hour with vocal and three-part backup for about 15-25 dollars.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Lovely. Let me take you back to that — you described working on demos. When you showed up to do a demo, what was usually presented to you? Was there a written out vocal line or was someone just sort of like singing it to you?
Well a written lead sheet with just the chords and the melody and lyrics. And in an hour, bass, piano, drums, guitar, I’d sing the vocal and then also do a three part back-up. Finished in an hour.
So that little five piece vocal ensemble paid off for you.
And how much did they pay?
I think it was 25 dollars maybe. Maybe it was 15 and 5 for each overdub. Because you were still going reel-to-reel.
